lines.trans: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday—and Wednesday at three o'clock the city clerk walks in!
Sit down and drink your hot coffee before you spill it, Mazen.
Look at our whiteboard: three days, three simple jobs.
Only three jobs?! Yesterday Room Nine was full of dust and silent piano keys!
Sunday: wash every window and read your aunt's old green guest book.
Monday: paint the outside shutters warm green and arrange twelve chairs.
Tuesday: repair the silent piano key and bake Wednesday's lemon tarts!
When you divide a mountain into three small hills, I can breathe again!
Where did you put that old green guest book from the attic, Mazen?
Right here under my arm! Wait—where did I put my coffee cup?
In your left hand, Mazen.
Go rest for ten minutes, boss—Nour and Suad will read the book!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Used in تحت إبطي ('tucked under my arm') when carrying books or newspapers.

examples.text: مازن كان حامل الدفتر الأخضر تحت إبطه.
examples.trans: Mazen was carrying the green ledger under his arm.

examples.text: حط الجريدة تحت إبطه ومشي عالسوق.
examples.trans: He tucked the newspaper under his arm and walked to the market.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برتاح, بيرتاح).

examples.trans: Rest up after your journey, ma'am.
We rested in the courtyard with a glass of tea.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'twelve'; before a singular counted noun it takes -r: اطنعشر دقة ('twelve chimes').

examples.trans: The clock tower chimed twelve!
Here is twelve dinars change.

meanings.note: First working day of the Jordanian week (pronounced il-ahad).

examples.text: يوم الأحد الصبح بنرتب جدول الأسبوع كله.
examples.trans: On Sunday morning we plan the schedule for the whole week.

examples.text: المدارس والمكاتب بعمان بتفتح يوم الأحد.
examples.trans: Schools and offices in Amman open on Sunday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: He called us on Tuesday.
The corner shop is open every Tuesday.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of الاثنين ('Monday', and with ال also 'both / the two').

examples.trans: I started work on Monday morning.
Monday's bus arrived at seven.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Baked fruit or custard tart, especially تارت الليمون ('lemon tart').

examples.text: تارت الليمون بقشرة اللوز طلع أطيب واحد.
examples.trans: The lemon tart with the almond crust turned out to be the tastiest one.

examples.text: خلينا قطعة تارت صغيرة لطارق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We saved a small slice of tart for Tariq in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Small hill (plural تلال tilaal); familiar across hilly Amman.

examples.text: عمان مبنية على تلال حلوة بتطل عالسما.
examples.trans: Amman is built across lovely hills looking out at the sky.

examples.text: لما نقسم الشغل الكبير لتلال صغيرة بصير سهل.
examples.trans: When we break a big job into small hills, it becomes easy.

meanings.note: Form V verb from نفس ('breath').

examples.text: فتحت الشباك عشان أتنفس هوا نضيف.
examples.trans: I opened the window to breathe fresh air.

examples.text: بعد ما رتبنا القائمة، قدرت أتنفس براحة.
examples.trans: Once we organized the list, I could breathe easily.

meanings.note: Means 'mountain' and also names Amman's historic hilltop quarters (جبل اللويبدة, جبل عمان).

examples.text: الهوا على راس الجبل دايما نضيف ومنعش.
examples.trans: The air on top of the mountain is always clean and crisp.

examples.text: بيت الياسمين قريب من درج الجبل القديم.
examples.trans: Jasmine Courtyard House is near the old Jabal stairway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: Describes outer shutters, doors, or walls facing the courtyard or street.

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش الخارجي بلون أخضر دافي.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the outside shutters a warm green.

examples.text: الباب الخارجي بيفتح مباشرة على شارع الياسمين.
examples.trans: The exterior gate opens straight onto Jasmine Street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

دخل.gloss: to enter; come in; go in

meanings.en: to enter; come in; go in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدخل, بيدخل).

examples.text: تفضل ادخل من المطر يا أستاذ.
examples.trans: Please come in out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برتب, بيرتب).

examples.trans: Life arranges sweeter melodies than we do.
I straighten my ties and keys every day.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: From سكت, to fall silent: a person who says nothing, or a thing that makes no sound.

examples.trans: Why are you so quiet today? Is something wrong?
The phone has been silent since the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشرب, بيشرب).

examples.trans: Drink hot tea first.

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من شوربة الخضار.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the vegetable soup.

meanings.note: Versatile spoken Levantine noun meaning 'task / job / matter'.

examples.text: ضل علينا تلات شغلات بسيطة قبل يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: We only have three simple tasks left before Wednesday.

examples.text: تذوق الكيك هو أحلى شغلة بالكافيه كله!
examples.trans: Tasting cake is the best job in the entire café!

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Levantine word for slatted window shutters, used as a collective: الشيش مسكر 'the shutters are closed'.

examples.trans: Close the shutters, the sun is strong.
Green shutters suit the house.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصلح, بيصلح).

examples.trans: I fix pipes and chairs.
Yesterday you fixed the old heater.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: ضيفة). Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: علالي.

examples.trans: The attic room on the third floor is sunny.
We brought the boxes down from the attic.

meanings.note: Arabic distinguishes father's sister (عمة, feminine of عمّ) from mother's sister (خالة).

examples.text: عمتي كانت تعزف عالبيانو كل يوم جمعة.
examples.trans: My paternal aunt used to play the piano every Friday.

examples.text: هاد الدفتر الأخضر هدية من عمتي.
examples.trans: This green notebook is a gift from my aunt.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate.
The shelves are clean with no dust on them.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Wash dishes, clothes, windows or your hands.

examples.trans: I washed the cups and put them on the shelf.
Wash your hands before eating.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فناجين.

examples.trans: I set two teacups on the tray.
This is my favourite coffee cup.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Used for dividing tasks across days or cutting pastry into portions.

examples.text: قسمنا الشغل بيننا عشان نخلص بدري.
examples.trans: We divided the work among ourselves so we would finish early.
Salma divided the tart into even slices.

meanings.note: Past tense verb meaning to sit down, or sometimes to stay/remain in a place.

examples.trans: Please have a seat in the courtyard under the tree.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay the whole week.

meanings.note: The beloved beverage, often Arabic coffee or Turkish-style, and by extension a coffee shop.

examples.text: بتحبي قهوة مع هيل ولا شاي؟
examples.trans: Would you like cardamom coffee or tea?
Morning coffee is ready on the stove.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

كب.gloss: to spill; pour out; pour down (rain)

meanings.en: to spill; pour out; pour down (rain)
meanings.note: Quintessential Jordanian verb for spilling coffee, throwing out water, or rain pouring down (عم تكب مطر).

examples.text: امسك الفنجان منيح قبل ما تكب القهوة.
examples.trans: Hold the cup steady before you spill the coffee.

examples.text: السما بلشت تكب مطر بنص الليل.
examples.trans: The sky started pouring rain at midnight.

meanings.note: An everyday item of furniture for sitting.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'yesterday' (مبارح بالليل 'last night').

examples.trans: Look what arrived last night!
I booked the room by phone yesterday.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مليانة, plural: مليانين).

examples.trans: All the hotels on our street are full tonight!
The pot is full of hot mint tea.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: موظفة). Plural: موظفين.

examples.trans: I am the new receptionist at the guesthouse.
All the staff here are helpful and friendly.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
